title: Open restriction of ordinary tensor homology
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings on its open site, $A$ the underlying ring sheaf, and $U$ an open. Let $V=\operatorname{overFunctor}(A,U)$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. For every unbounded cochain complex $P$ of $A$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], sheaf $F$ of $A$-modules, and integer $i$, there is an isomorphism $V(H^i(\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R F[0])))\cong H^i(\operatorname{Tot}(V(P)\otimes_{R|_U}V(F)[0]))$, with homology as in [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules] and total tensor as in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. No K-flatness assumption is needed. The zero-map witness only constructs the termwise restriction functor.

source.place: Tag 03DH (sites-modules-section-localize); Tag 01CD (modules-lemma-tensor-product-pullback); local tensor calculation in Tag 0DJQ

proof.text: Restriction is additive on sectionwise maps. Compose it with the exact forgetful functor to abelian sheaves; this composite is the forgetful functor followed by overPullback. Finite-limit preservation of overPullback and reflection of limits by the module forgetful functor prove finite-limit preservation of restriction. Finite colimits are preserved because overFunctor is pushforward along the cocontinuous over-forgetful functor with identity ring map, a left adjoint. Thus restriction preserves homology.

For fixed F, specialize the natural tensor comparison to the pair (M,F) and its naturality to (f,id_F). This yields a natural isomorphism tensorRight(F) followed by V ≅ V followed by tensorRight(V(F)). Lift it to complexes by NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex and Functor.mapHomologicalComplexCompIso.

The proved CochainComplex.mapBifunctorSingle₂Iso in WeilConjectures.FromJoel.Algebra.Homology.BifunctorSingle identifies total tensor with F[0] with the termwise tensorRight(F) functor, on both sites. Compose its restriction, the lifted natural comparison, and the inverse single comparison on the localized site. Apply the homology functor and prepend the inverse of ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso to get exactly the asserted isomorphism. This proof never requires a bound on P or comparison of infinite coproducts.
